guitar.evidence: Mike Bloomfield was a famous blues-rock guitarist (Butterfield Blues Band, Super Session) well documented as a Gibson Les Paul player (notably a 1959 Les Paul) and earlier a Telecaster user; Al Kooper himself is primarily a keyboardist/organist on this track.
guitar.notes: Al Kooper plays organ on 'Albert's Shuffle'; Bloomfield is the guitarist of record.

tone.target: raw 60s blues-rock lead with nasal wah and edge-of-breakup grind
tone.profile: raw 60s blues-rock lead with nasal wah and edge-of-breakup grind
tone.summary: A gritty, vintage lead tone built around a small British combo amp (UK 45) and a Wah pedal, emphasizing mid-range bite and controlled breakup for a raw '60s feel.
corrections: make wah explicit as the signature effect
favor raw 60s texture over blues-rock vagueness

rig.name: Al Kooper & Mike Bloomfield - Albert's Shuffle - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide slight grit and mid-forward bite without sounding like modern overdrive.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate the gentle breakup of a vintage tube amp, fulfilling the 'slight fuzz/grit' requirement.

blocks.purpose: The signature wah sweep required for the '60s blues-rock lead' sound.
blocks.gap: While a dedicated Wah module is ideal, Red Haze (a filter/wah emulation) provides the necessary sweeping frequency control and bite.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the sound of a small British combo amp (Fender/small combo clue), providing mid-forward punch and vintage character.
Provide a classic, open-air British cabinet sound suitable for blues lead work.
Sculpt the tone by boosting the mid-range frequencies to achieve 'mid-forward bite' and cut.
Add the required 'light slapback' echo effect.
Provide a subtle sense of space and vintage depth without sounding 'lush' or ambient.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the dry, mid-forward punch of a vintage small combo amp.

proposals.recommendedAsset: vintage single-mic'd 1x or 2x cab IR (e.g., Fender Deluxe/Princeton)
proposals.reason: The current 4x12 is too large and loses the intimate, mid-focused sound of a small combo.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased vintage punch and focus on upper mids.
